report:
Conclusion: The difference (B − A) appears to be a bias that pushes completions toward example-style / identity-mapping and code-like continuations — i.e., a tendency to echo inputs or produce short paired examples / small code/list demonstrations.

Why I think so
- Patchscope: injecting the difference into an identity prompt repeatedly yields outputs like "cat -> cat", "1135 -> 1135", short python snippets, and phrases such as "This is a valid programming language", "This is a valid question", "This is a good start. You've successfully echoed the input." Those continuations strongly indicate an inclination to produce demo/example formats and literal echoing of tokens.
- Logit-lens: high-norm cells point at tokens common in demonstrations, list/code structure and instruction phrasing — e.g. "This", "try", "prepare", "optimize", ":" , "\n", code-like punctuation, and many plain word tokens that appear in short examples or headlines. Several high-scoring tokens are explicit single-token echoes or list markers (numbers, newline).
- Localization: the L2 difference is concentrated in late layers (especially layer 25 pos0, and many pos0/pos1 in layers ~18–25), which is consistent with an effect that alters final-token selection / generation style (how the model starts/frames its continuation).

Caveats / alternatives
- Some logit-lens tokens (e.g. "tragic", "iconic", "vivid", "colorful") are noisy and suggest partial overlap with other topical distributions (news/creative descriptions). But the patchscope readouts give a more direct behavioral signal (echoing / example completions), so I weigh that heavier.
- I cannot on this evidence pin down whether A or B is the “echoing” model (only that B − A has this direction). I also cannot say whether this comes from a specific training objective (e.g., an extra instruction/few-shot dataset) or just a distributional shift in fine-tuning — only that the difference manifests as increased example/identity-mapping style continuations.

If you want, I can: (a) test with targeted prompts to confirm echoing vs. other styles, (b) try to determine which checkpoint (A or B) exhibits the behavior, or (c) quantify how strongly the effect changes token probabilities for typical first tokens.
